title: embeddings-volume-smoothing-and-rerank-contract-qsa-prep
text:
embeddings-volume-smoothing-and-rerank-contract-qsa-prep

description:
Goal: design and run a compact pilot for a smoothing-oriented pricing option for embeddings and reranking that balances predictable revenue with unit economics friendly to high-volume customers, and prepare enterprise contract language + security questionnaire artifacts for QSA review. Scope: (1) propose 2 pricing variants and associated billing meter semantics, (2) define pilot criteria and customer cohorts, (3) produce legal/contract language templates for commits and SLAs, (4) answer & map security questionnaire items tied to price tiers. Success metrics: pilot ARR uplift >= $150k/year from participating accounts, 10% reduction in per-vector cost for targeted workloads via batching/commit behaviors, <5% billing disputes during pilot.

comments:
2025-02-13 Monica Reyes: Initial scoping doc uploaded to Confluence. Outlined two candidate approaches: A) Tiered slab with soft smoothing (price per 1M vectors decreases after thresholds with automatic smoothing for month-to-month variance) and B) Rolling commitment model (customers commit to monthly rolling volume at discounted per-unit rate with overage and burst credit rules).
2025-02-17 Liam Patel (Sales): Sales feedback: Sales prefers model B for enterprise conversations because it maps cleanly to existing revenue recognition and helps negotiate multi-quarter discounts. Concern about billing complexity for burst credits — asked for a simple example invoice line item format.
2025-02-21 Engineering review (Ethan Clarke): ENG notes: accurate metering for rerank vs embedding calls will require adding a 'vector-unit-weight' label to request events and a short-lived aggregation service to produce daily aggregates. Rough estimate: 2 sprints of backend work (ENG-29117). Also flagged potential high-cardinality issues for customers with many projects — propose grouping by account-level meter key.
2025-02-25 Finance (Priya Singh): Modeling results: Variant A (Tiered slab) shows higher short-term gross margin but worse NRR for accounts with spiky usage. Variant B (Rolling commitment) shows more predictable ARR and lower disputes but needs contract language for minimum term. Modeled ARR uplift for a 6-customer pilot = $180k/year for variant B vs $120k/year for variant A. Documented assumptions in the pricing model spreadsheet.
2025-02-28 Legal (Amir Novak): Draft contract clauses requested: commit definitions, overage pricing grace period, termination and credit reconciliation flow. Also requested that we prepare a security questionnaire appendix that maps price tiers to allowed deployment modes (hosted only vs dedicated/private) and required SOC/ISO attestations. Legal created ticket LEG-331 for T&Cs edits.
2025-03-03 Compliance (Juli Chen): QSA prep: flagged three SSF items that need clarifying for discounted commitment tiers — data residency commitments for private deployments, encryption-at-rest key ownership, and audit log retention. Asked for a short appendix mapping answers per tier. Assigned to me (Monica) and Ethan for technical writeups.
2025-03-04 Monica Reyes: Decision checkpoint — move forward with Variant B (Rolling commitment) as the pilot offering. Next steps: 1) finalize technical acceptance criteria with ENG (ENG-29117), 2) Legal to draft pilot contract template and QSA appendix (LEGAL-331), 3) Sales to identify 3 candidate pilot customers and sign LOIs by 2025-03-21, 4) Billing to prototype meter aggregation and an invoice preview by 2025-03-18. Added to Cycle 47 board for visibility.
2025-03-04 Ethan Clarke: Engineering notes added to comment thread: agree to two-sprint runway. We will implement a daily aggregation job that emits per-account committed vs consumed totals and a pilot-only invoice preview endpoint. Will add detailed tech design PR under ENG-29117 and link to this ticket when ready.

acceptance_criteria:
Billing system can produce daily and monthly committed vs consumed aggregates per account (pilot customers)
Legal approved pilot contract with explicit commit/overage language and QSA appendix for price tiers
Sales signed LOIs with 3 customers representing at least $150k ARR in combined commits
Pilot telemetry dashboard in Console showing per-customer effective RPM, batch-hit rate, and invoice preview
